C1-01.title: Before the serve: where to stand
C1-01.scene: It's your serve. Your partner is at the net on the left.
C1-01.cue: The right half of our court is open.
C1-01.question: Where do you serve from?

answer.why: Your partner has the left, so the right is yours. Stand wider than in singles.
answer.caption: You can reach the wide return too

lo.why: That's the singles spot. Good serve angle, but the right sideline is open.
lo.caption: The right side is too far away

hi.why: Foot fault. You always serve from behind the baseline.
hi.caption: Foot fault!

C1-01.coach: Serve from behind the line, in the middle of the right half.
C1-01.next: After the serve: stay back or come in?

C1-02.title: The net player's starting spot
C1-02.scene: Your partner is getting ready to serve from the back right.
C1-02.cue: You're standing near the service line.
C1-02.question: Where do you stand?

answer.short: Two or three steps off the net
answer.why: From here you can move forward or back. Too close and you're weak to lobs; too far and you're weak on volleys.
answer.caption: You put the volley away

lo.why: Safe against lobs, but you've given up the net.
lo.caption: It drops at your feet

hi.short: In the middle from the start
hi.why: The middle is where you go after the serve lands. Stand there early and your alley opens.
hi.caption: Beaten down the alley

C1-02.coach: The middle isn't where you stand — it's where you go.
C1-02.next: The serve is in — when do you move?

C1-03.title: When to poach
C1-03.scene: Your partner's wide serve pulled the returner out wide.
C1-03.question: How do you move?

answer.why: A stretched returner usually plays the safe crosscourt. The middle is right in its path.
answer.caption: Picked it off — point!

lo.why: Safe, but the opponents keep hitting easy crosscourts.
lo.caption: The easy crosscourts keep coming

hi.short: Back off to guard the line
hi.why: Down the line is the hardest shot to hit anyway. Guarding it leaves the middle open.
hi.caption: Beaten through the middle

C1-03.coach: The net player eats the middle, not the line.
C1-03.next: After a poach, you switch sides

C1-04.title: Setting up to return
C1-04.scene: Returning in the ad court (left). It's your turn.
C1-04.cue: The server is standing close to the sideline.
C1-04.question: Where do you return from?

answer.why: When the server stands wide, the serve angles go wide too. Stand in the middle of those angles.
answer.caption: You get the wide serve back too

lo.why: Right direction. But it's too close for a first serve — you react late.
lo.caption: Late, and the ball floats

hi.why: One wide serve and you can't even touch it.
hi.caption: You gave up an ace

C1-04.coach: When the server stands wide, you stand wide.
C1-04.next: You're set — where do you hit it?

C1-05.title: Where the returner's partner stands
C1-05.scene: Your partner is getting ready to return from the right.
C1-05.cue: You're right up at the net.
C1-05.question: Where should you stand?

answer.why: You don't know yet how the return will go. Stand where you can go forward or back.
answer.caption: Standing back, you blocked it

lo.why: Great if the return is good — but if it floats, you're the smash target.
lo.caption: You barely block the smash

hi.why: If you're both back, you hand over the whole front court. Too far back for a starting spot.
hi.caption: The front was open — point lost

C1-05.coach: When you don't know yet, stand where you can go either way.
C1-05.next: You're set — where do you look?

C1-06.title: Where do your eyes go?
C1-06.scene: The serve is on its way to your partner.
C1-06.cue: The opposing net player hasn't moved yet.
C1-06.question: What do you watch right now?

answer.why: Your partner hits this ball. If the net player moves, the ball comes to you.
answer.caption: You saw the poach and blocked it

lo.why: It's instinct, but you don't need to watch that ball.
lo.caption: Late, but you get there

hi.why: The ball has already left. You're watching someone who's done.
hi.caption: Caught by the poach

C1-06.coach: Don't watch the ball — watch the person who's about to move.
C1-06.next: Good return — do you move in?

C1-07.title: After the serve: stay back or come in?
C1-07.scene: You've served. The returner got set in time.
C1-07.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: The return is coming back properly. Stay put and get ready for the third ball.
answer.caption: The third ball is easy too

lo.short: Come in a step or two
lo.why: Not bad, but against a deep return you'll be hitting while backing up.
lo.caption: Hitting while backing up

hi.short: Run in to the service line
hi.why: If the returner hits it well, the service line is at your feet — the hardest spot to play from.
hi.caption: It landed at your feet

C1-07.coach: When the return comes back well, stay behind the line.

C1-08.title: Where to return a first serve
C1-08.scene: A fast first serve. You can barely get your racket on it.
C1-08.cue: The opposing net player is in the middle of the box.
C1-08.question: Where do you return it?

answer.why: The net is lowest and the court is longest. It's also farthest from the net player.
answer.caption: The server gets pushed back

lo.why: Right direction. But short lets the server step in and attack.
lo.caption: The server steps in and attacks

hi.why: The net player can reach it just by stretching. The net is highest there, too.
hi.caption: The net player picked it off

C1-08.coach: When you're rushed, use the longest part of the court.
C1-08.next: What if the net player moves?

C1-09.title: Your partner got pulled wide
C1-09.scene: Your partner was pulled out wide right. The back left of our court is open.
C1-09.cue: A floater is coming at chest height.
C1-09.question: Where do you send it?

answer.why: A short ball in the middle has to be lifted. From that, they can't aim at our gap.
answer.caption: Dropped it short

lo.why: Safe, but it buys the opponents time to get set.
lo.caption: They bought themselves time

hi.why: The net player is in the way, and if they angle it back, our side is open.
hi.caption: It came back to the open side

C1-09.coach: When our court is open, take away the angles first.

C1-10.title: Your partner poached
C1-10.scene: A rally after your serve. Your partner charged the middle.
C1-10.cue: The left side of our court is empty.
C1-10.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: A poach means you two switch sides. Fill the spot your partner left.
answer.caption: You filled the gap

lo.short: Shift a little to the middle
lo.why: Right direction, but you can't reach the left sideline from there.
lo.caption: You barely get there

hi.why: If the poach gets blocked, the ball comes to the empty left.
hi.caption: Beaten to the empty left

C1-10.coach: A poach means you two switch sides.
C1-10.next: Where does the poaching partner go?

C1-11.title: Two returns down the line
C1-11.scene: Your partner is serving. You're the net player.
C1-11.cue: Two returns went down the line — both out.
C1-11.question: Where do you stand this time?

answer.why: Both were out. Keep half an eye on the alley and guard the middle, where they actually hit well.
answer.caption: You picked off a ball in the middle

lo.why: That's more pressure, but the alley opens even more. No reason to change.
lo.caption: You barely cover the alley

hi.why: Guarding the shot they keep missing leaves the middle open.
hi.caption: The middle was open

C1-11.coach: The shot they want and the shot they can hit are different.

C1-12.title: The net player moved
C1-12.scene: A second serve is coming. You're the returner.
C1-12.cue: The opposing net player ran to the middle.
C1-12.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.short: Down the line, where they left
answer.why: The moment the net player leaves, down the line becomes the shortest, emptiest shot.
answer.caption: Through the gap they left

lo.why: Right direction. But short lets the net player take a step back and cover.
lo.caption: The net player got back to cover

hi.why: That's exactly where the net player just ran.
hi.caption: Caught by the poach

C1-12.coach: Only go down the line after the net player moves.
C1-12.next: What about when we're the net player?

C1-13.title: The gap between you two
C1-13.scene: Your ball went to the middle of their court. Not very deep.
C1-13.cue: You're far right; your partner is front left.
C1-13.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: If the ball is in the middle, their angles are in the middle too. It also closes the gap to your partner.
answer.caption: You covered the middle

lo.why: You've just split the court in half. A ball down the middle and you both hesitate.
lo.caption: You run and barely get it

hi.why: Coming in behind a ball that isn't deep gets you a ball at your feet.
hi.caption: Missed the ball at your feet

C1-13.coach: You and your partner move together, like you're tied with a rope.
C1-13.next: What if your partner gets pushed back?

C1-14.title: Your partner got pushed back
C1-14.scene: Your partner was pushed behind the baseline and barely got it over.
C1-14.cue: Our ball is high and slow.
C1-14.question: What do you do?

answer.why: A short floater invites a smash. The farther back you are, the more time you have.
answer.caption: You stepped back and got it back

lo.short: Back to the service line only
lo.why: Backing off is right — but you're still too close to handle a smash.
lo.caption: You barely got a racket on it

hi.why: The floater gets smashed down at your feet.
hi.caption: Smashed down at your feet

C1-14.coach: When your partner is pushed back, you back off too.
C1-14.next: The signal to move up again

C1-15.title: After the poach: go back?
C1-15.scene: You ran to the middle and cut off the return.
C1-15.cue: Your partner has already crossed to the left.
C1-15.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: Your partner already filled the left. If you go back, you're both on one side.
answer.caption: You held the right

lo.why: That spot covers neither side. You're half a beat late both ways.
lo.caption: Half a beat late

hi.why: You end up on the same side as your partner. The whole right is open.
hi.caption: The right was wide open

C1-15.coach: When you poach, you switch sides. Don't go back.
C1-15.next: A lob comes — who takes it?

C1-16.title: A good return
C1-16.scene: Your partner's return landed at the server's feet.
C1-16.cue: The server bends low and lifts it.
C1-16.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: A lifted ball floats. A floater is easiest to put away up at the net.
answer.caption: You put away the floater

lo.why: You're a step late, so you play it from below instead of hitting down.
lo.caption: You just get it back over

hi.why: Someone lifting the ball can't hit hard. Backing off means you can't reach the short ball.
hi.caption: You couldn't reach the short ball

C1-16.coach: When they lift it, you move up.

C1-17.title: The return floated
C1-17.scene: This time your partner's return floated high.
C1-17.cue: The opposing net player raises the racket overhead.
C1-17.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: This ball is coming down hard from above. Distance gives you time to react.
answer.caption: Distance let you get it back

lo.why: Backing off is right. But it opens your side.
lo.caption: Your side was open

hi.why: Blocking a smash right at the net is hard even for pros.
hi.caption: You became the smash target

C1-17.coach: When our ball floats, you back off.
C1-17.next: After you block it, get back in position

C1-18.title: A deep crosscourt return
C1-18.scene: The return came back deep crosscourt. You have time to set up.
C1-18.cue: The opposing net player is in the middle of the box.
C1-18.question: Where do you send it?

answer.why: It's farthest from the net player and the safest shot. Whoever changes direction first is at a disadvantage.
answer.caption: They broke down first

lo.why: A good shot — but with the net player standing there, it's within reach.
lo.caption: The net player got a racket on it

hi.why: Aiming at their feet from far back makes the ball float — right at racket height.
hi.caption: You gifted them a floater

C1-18.coach: Go at their feet from close in. From far back, it's a gift.
C1-18.next: What if they switch to a lob?

C1-19.title: A lob over your head
C1-19.scene: The return was lobbed over your head.
C1-19.cue: The ball is dropping into our back left.
C1-19.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: Your partner chases the ball. You fill the open right. Say it out loud.
answer.caption: You filled the gap and held

lo.short: Only as far as the middle
lo.why: You went halfway. The right sideline is still open.
lo.caption: You went halfway and were late

hi.why: If your partner comes behind you, you're both on the left.
hi.caption: The right was open

C1-19.coach: A ball over your head is the signal to cross over.
C1-19.next: After the switch, the next ball?

C1-20.title: The ball after the switch
C1-20.scene: Switch done. Your partner just got it back — short and high.
C1-20.cue: The opposing net player is setting up to smash.
C1-20.question: Where will they hit it?

answer.why: You're front right, your partner back left. The gap between you is the biggest hole.
answer.caption: You read it and got there first

lo.why: The net player's feet are a good target too. But right now the gap between you is bigger.
lo.caption: Your partner barely blocks it

hi.short: To your partner at the back
hi.why: The deep spot is where your partner is waiting. The smash won't go there.
hi.caption: It went right between you

C1-20.coach: If you're standing diagonally, the smash goes through the gap.

C1-21.title: They're hitting from the corner
C1-21.scene: Your angled (short and wide) volley pulled an opponent out to the left.
C1-21.cue: The opponent is stretching from outside the court.
C1-21.question: Where do you stand?

answer.short: Toward the ball, to the left
answer.why: From the corner, the angles they can hit are narrow. Just stand inside those angles.
answer.caption: You waited inside the angle

lo.why: Not wrong, but you're shaded right of the real angle.
lo.caption: Half a beat late

hi.why: Your partner has the back right. If you go too, the left opens up.
hi.caption: Beaten on the left

C1-21.coach: Don't guard the court — guard the angles they can actually hit.
C1-21.next: They barely got it back — finish it

C1-22.title: You picked off the poach — where to?
C1-22.scene: Poach worked. You can hit it in the middle at chest height.
C1-22.cue: The returner is in the corner; their net player is in the box.
C1-22.question: Where do you send it?

answer.why: That's the biggest hole right now. It drops while they wait for each other.
answer.caption: Finished it between them

lo.why: A good shot, but you aimed at a person when a bigger gap was open.
lo.caption: The net player reflexed it back

hi.why: That's toward where they're standing, and the corner is the smallest target.
hi.caption: Went for the corner — out

C1-22.coach: Finish between the two of them, not with power.
C1-22.next: What if they barely float it back?

C1-23.title: Standing diagonally
C1-23.scene: Mid-rally, you notice you two are standing diagonally.
C1-23.cue: The gap between you is the widest it can be.
C1-23.question: What do you do?

answer.why: Diagonal means the longest gap between you. Closing in shuts the hole in the middle.
answer.caption: You closed the middle

lo.why: That tidies the formation, but you give up the net. Save it for when you're pushed back.
lo.caption: You give up the net and hang on

hi.why: Your partner is busy hitting from the back and can't come up. The hole stays open.
hi.caption: Beaten through the diagonal gap

C1-23.coach: When you're diagonal, whoever can move goes first.
C1-23.next: If they float it, who hits it?

C1-24.title: A floater down the middle: who takes it?
C1-24.scene: The opponents barely got it back and popped it up.
C1-24.cue: The ball is coming down between you two.
C1-24.question: Who hits it?

answer.why: A floater down the middle belongs to whoever is closer to the net — hit down on it.
answer.caption: The front player finished it

lo.why: Hitting on the run, your footwork won't line up — and you're just standing there.
lo.caption: They ran in and barely got it over

hi.why: The most common way to lose a point. Decide in advance and it goes away.
hi.caption: You both watched it go by

C1-24.coach: A floater down the middle belongs to the player in front.
